question.:question/problem: Which of the following diagrams gives the slope field at the points indicated for the differential equation $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=(-2)\frac{y^{2}}{x}?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
We have to sketch the slope field at the points $(3,1)$,$(-3,-3)$,$(-1,-1)$.

To sketch the slope field at the given points, we substitute their coordinates into the right-hand side of the differential equation.

$$
\begin{aligned} & {\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{(3,1)}=(-2)\frac{(1)^{2}}{(3)}=- \frac{2}{3}, \\  & {\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{(-3,-3)}=(-2)\frac{(-3)^{2}}{(-3)}=6, \\  & {\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{(-1,-1)}=(-2)\frac{(-1)^{2}}{(-1)}=2.\end{aligned}
$$

Setting up our points and drawing our line segments, we get the following diagram.
